terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Merge summer-sale into main
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. It is July, and the summer sale can go on the site. `main` has not moved since `summer-sale` started from it.

Merge `summer-sale` into `main`. Because `main` has nothing new of its own, Git only has to move `main` forward to the last commit of the sale: no merge commit.

The check expects both commits of the sale on `main`'s own line of history, with no merge commit for them.
nextSteps: Run `git log --oneline --graph --all` and find where each branch points.
Make sure `git status` says `On branch main`.
Merge `summer-sale` and read what Git prints: it says `Fast-forward`.
Look at the graph again: `main` and `summer-sale` point at the same commit.
hints: A merge brings another branch into the branch you are on, so be on main.
`git merge` takes the name of the branch to bring in.

tasks.title: Merge reading-group into main, with a merge commit
tasks.description:
Now merge `reading-group`, with Wilma's July book, into `main`. `main` has moved on since that branch started, so Git joins the two lines with a merge commit. Git writes its message for you, and you can keep it as it is.

The check looks on `main`'s own line for a merge commit that brings in the reading group book, and expects no merge left half done.
nextSteps: Run `git log --oneline --graph --all`: `reading-group` started from an older commit than `main`'s last one.
Merge `reading-group` on `main`, keeping Git's message without an editor.
If an editor opens anyway, close it as the lesson says, keeping the message.
Run `git log --oneline --graph -n 5`: two lines meet in the merge commit.
hints: Git makes a merge commit when both branches have commits the other does not. Like any commit, it needs a message.
One option of git merge keeps the message Git writes and opens no editor.

tasks.title: Delete the branches that are merged
tasks.description:
Read the graph with `git log --oneline --graph --all`. Every commit of `summer-sale` and of `reading-group` is now in `main`, so those two branches can go. `window-display` holds a commit `main` does not have, and Wilma has not decided about it: keep it.

Delete the two merged branches. The check expects `summer-sale` and `reading-group` to be gone with all their commits in `main`, and `window-display` to be still there.
nextSteps: Run `git log --oneline --graph --all` and see which branch names sit on commits that are in `main`.
Delete those branches with the safe way the lesson shows.
If Git refuses, read why: it means the branch has commits `main` does not have.
hints: Deleting a branch deletes only the name. The commits stay, as long as another branch holds them.
`git branch` lists, makes and deletes branches. The lower-case option deletes only a branch that is merged.
